takes.label: Talking head, raw Seedance output (480p)
takes.prompt:
SCENE CONTEXT
A living oil-painted self-portrait. A man in a brown fedora, positioned slightly left of center in front of a pale plaster wall with a tall window frame at right and a warm brown wooden ledge at lower right, speaks two short lines directly to the viewer, leans in a little between them, and ends holding his stare.

ACTIVE REFERENCES
<<<image_1>>>: man in his late 40s, long face, heavy-lidded dark eyes, full reddish lips, brown felt fedora with a dark band, cobalt-blue shirt, dark olive tie, charcoal-black jacket. Rendered as thick oil paint with visible brushstrokes on every surface, including his skin. Voice: low, slow, dry American baritone with a flat upstate New York accent, unhurried. 100% matches the reference.

FIRST FRAME / BLOCKING
Exactly <<<image_1>>>: head and upper chest, body turned three-quarters toward frame right, head turned back toward the lens, face in the upper-middle of the frame, gaze straight into camera.

FORMAT MODE
One continuous shot, the camera does not cut on its own.

OPTICS
MCU at 29° portrait compression for the whole shot, no drift.

CAMERA
Locked off at eye level, face in sharp focus throughout. All movement comes from him.

ACTION
0.0s to 2.0s — he holds still, takes one slow breath through the nose, blinks once slowly.
2.0s to 5.0s — he speaks, calm and matter-of-fact, at an unhurried pace: "You walked past that diner a hundred times."
5.0s to 6.5s — silence. He leans slowly toward the lens by about 3 cm, chin dipping slightly so the hat brim lowers a little; his eyes stay locked on the lens.
6.5s to 8.5s — he speaks, quieter, almost confidential: "Tomorrow, you go inside."
8.5s to 10.0s — he holds the stare into the lens, lips closed, perfectly still; one corner of his mouth tightens very slightly.

PERFORMANCE
Restraint and economy. Clear, accurate lip-sync with small, natural jaw movement, every word visibly shaped by the lips. Brow heavy and level. Wet catch-light in both eyes. Breathing visible in the shoulders. He moves like living paint: the brushstrokes on his face, hat and jacket travel with every movement and keep their texture.

LIGHTING
Soft, even daylight from frame left at 5200K. Warm light on the left side of his face, gentle shadow on his right cheek and under the hat brim; as he leans in, the brim shadow deepens slightly across his brow. Flat, even light on the wall. Exposure constant for the whole shot.

AUDIO
His voice only, close-miked and dry, over a quiet room tone. The second line is slightly softer and closer than the first.

STYLE
A painted portrait come to life: thick impasto brush texture, matte canvas, the muted palette of cream plaster, cobalt shirt, charcoal jacket, warm brown felt and brown wood. Every frame reads as oil on canvas.

POSITIVE LOCKS
Fedora, shirt, tie, jacket, window frame, wooden ledge and wall stay identical throughout. He keeps his three-quarter pose and position; the lean is small and slow. His gaze stays on the lens from 2.0s to the end. Oil-paint texture on every frame, start to finish.

Sound: the hum of the fluorescent light and the coffee urn, coffee pouring, a faint radio playing a slow 1940s jazz ballad, the scratch and flare of the match. Only the two spoken lines.
